subject: DI05019021

h.en: 5.1.1 Hydrogen:energy carrier, not a primary source

body.en:
Definition / principle

Hydrogen stores/transports energy obtained from a production process; its benefits depend on the full pathway.

Understand why

High energy per unit mass contrasts with low ambient energy per unit volume; storage and transport can dominate the system design.

Classify separately by production route, energy/emissions label, storage form and end use.

End uses include feedstock, industrial reduction, combustion and fuel cells; not every use is equally efficient or practical.

Does tailpipe water prove green hydrogen?

No. The production pathway and emissions boundary matter.
body.gu:
Definition / Principle

Hydrogen production processની energy store/transport કરે;લાભ full pathway પર આધારિત.

કારણ સાથે સમજીએ

High energy/mass સામે low ambient energy/volume;storage,transport system designમાં મહત્વના.

Feedstock,industrial reduction,combustion,fuel cells uses;બધા equally efficient/practical નહિ.

Tailpipe Waterથી Green Hydrogen સાબિત?

ના.Production pathway,emissions boundary મહત્વની.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Green refers to an appropriately renewable-based production pathway meeting the applicable emissions definition—not merely water at the exhaust.

Understand why

Grey commonly denotes fossil-based production without capture; blue adds carbon capture; pink often denotes nuclear-linked electrolysis; labels can vary.

Renewable electricity electrolysis is one green route; qualifying biomass-based routes may also be recognised under a given standard.

Assess electricity/feedstock origin, upstream emissions, water treatment, purification and compression within the specified boundary.

Blue is not automatically zero carbon and electrolysis with carbon-intensive electricity is not automatically green.
body.gu:
Definition / Principle

Green એટલે suitable renewable-based production,applicable emissions definition;ફક્ત exhaustમાં water નહિ.

કારણ સાથે સમજીએ

Grey સામાન્ય fossil without capture;blue carbon capture સાથે;pink ઘણી વાર nuclear-linked electrolysis;labels vary.

Renewable electricity electrolysis એક green route;given standardમાં qualifying biomass routes પણ માન્ય હોઈ શકે.

Specified boundaryમાં electricity/feedstock origin,upstream emissions,water treatment,purification,compression જુઓ.

Blue automatically zero carbon નહિ;carbon-intensive electricity electrolysis automatically green નહિ.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Compressed H2 is high-pressure gas; liquid H2 is cryogenic liquid near20K(about−253°C).

Classification / types — basis first

  • Physical storage:compressed gas and cryogenic liquid; material storage/carriers are separate routes. Compressed H2 remains gas; liquid H2 is near20K(about−253°C).

Construction — each part and its purpose

  1. Compressed storage uses approved pressure vessels, compatible liners/overwrap where designed, valves and rated connections.
  2. Isolation, monitoring, pressure protection and engineered vent routing belong to the complete gas-storage system.
  3. Cryogenic storage uses an inner vessel, outer jacket and high-performance insulation, often an evacuated insulating space.
  4. Liquid/gas outlets, instrumentation and approved relief/boil-off management handle normal heat ingress and abnormal pressure.
  5. Materials, seals and supports must match pressure, H2 compatibility and thermal contraction rather than copying an ordinary tank.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Compressed storage receives gas through an authorised engineered system and retains it at the rated operating conditions; representative vehicle classes include350/700 bar, not instructions for filling.
  2. During use, approved pressure reduction/conditioning supplies the required downstream duty without treating storage pressure as injector pressure.
  3. Liquefaction requires prior energy input; insulated storage limits but cannot abolish ambient heat transfer.
  4. Heat ingress may produce boil-off; engineered pressure/vent management handles it while the specified product is withdrawn.
  5. Compare useful delivered capacity, system mass, volume, holding time, losses and conditioning energy—not only fuel mass.

Application / advantages

Gas avoids liquefaction; liquid offers higher volumetric density where the energy and cryogenic infrastructure are justified.

Common mistake / conditions

Pressure hazards, embrittlement/permeation and cryogenic cold-burn/boil-off hazards demand approved design. No DIY storage, pressurisation or transfer procedure is provided.

body.en:
Definition / principle

State the process before discussing its colour label or carbon claim.

Understand why

Electrochemical:water electrolysis using supplied electricity; thermochemical:reforming, gasification or pyrolysis with suitable feedstocks and heat.

Biological and photoelectrochemical routes are other families at differing stages of development.

Reforming commonly yields a hydrogen-containing mixture requiring shift/purification; carbon management depends on the process.

Compare feedstock, energy demand, maturity, purity, water use, cost and lifecycle emissions rather than listing colours as chemical processes.

h.gu: 5.4.2 Production Routes:દરેકમાં Hydrogen કેવી રીતે મળે?

body.en:
Definition / principle

A colour label is not a production mechanism; follow feedstock, conversion and separation.

Understand why

Steam reforming:hydrocarbon and steam form a H2-containing gas; for methane, CH4+H2O→CO+3H2 is the main reforming reaction in the simplified model.

Water-gas shift:CO+H2O→CO2+H2 increases hydrogen; separation/purification supplies the required product purity. Carbon capture changes emissions management, not this basic need for purification.

Gasification converts suitable solid/biomass feedstock into a mixed synthesis gas; cleaning, shift and separation may follow, so raw syngas is not pure hydrogen.

Methane pyrolysis conceptually splits CH4→C+2H2; heat source, solid-carbon handling and upstream methane leakage affect the pathway assessment.

Electrolysis splits water using electricity; biological/photoelectrochemical approaches use different mechanisms and maturity levels. Cost, purity and lifecycle performance must be compared on one boundary.
body.gu:
Definition / Principle

Colour label production mechanism નથી;feedstock,conversion,separation follow કરો.

કારણ સાથે સમજીએ

Steam reformingમાં hydrocarbon,steamથી H2-containing gas;simple methane modelમાં CH4+H2O→CO+3H2.

Water-gas shift CO+H2O→CO2+H2થી hydrogen વધે;separation/purification required purity આપે.Carbon capture purificationની જરૂર દૂર નહિ કરે.

Gasification suitable solid/biomassથી mixed syngas બનાવે;cleaning,shift,separation હોઈ શકે;raw syngas pure hydrogen નહિ.

Methane pyrolysis concept CH4→C+2H2;heat source,solid-carbon handling,upstream leakage assessment બદલે.

Electrolysis electricityથી water split કરે;biological/photoelectrochemical mechanisms,maturity જુદી.Cost,purity,lifecycle performance એક boundaryમાં compare કરો.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Electrical energy drives water splitting; the overall reaction is2H2O→2H2+O2.

Classification / types — basis first

  • Alkaline:liquid alkaline electrolyte and suitable separator; hydroxide-ion transfer.
  • PEM:proton-conducting polymer membrane; protons pass from anode to cathode.
  • Solid-oxide/high-temperature:ceramic electrolyte with the specified ion chemistry and steam/heat integration.
  • AEM:anion-exchange-membrane route, with its own material and maturity considerations.
  • The detailed representative below is PEM; the following comparison card explains why the other constructions/ion paths differ.

Construction — each part and its purpose

  1. A DC power supply/power converter feeds the cell stack; it must be distinguished from renewable generation upstream.
  2. Anode and cathode catalyst/electrode layers support oxygen- and hydrogen-evolution reactions in the representative PEM electrolyser.
  3. Proton membrane conducts ions and separates gases; current collectors/flow plates distribute current, water and gas.
  4. Water treatment and feed maintain the cell's required purity; not every raw-water source may enter directly.
  5. Gas-liquid separation, drying/purification as required and distinct H2/O2 outlets condition the products without combining them.
  6. Cooling, sensors, pressure management, venting and protective shutdown support the engineered plant.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Electricity supplies energy for a non-spontaneous water-splitting process; water reaches the approved cell feed path.
  2. In PEM electrolysis, the anode reaction is H2O→1/2O2+2H+ +2e−.
  3. Protons cross the membrane while electrons move through the powered external circuit, not through the membrane.
  4. At the cathode,2H+ +2e−→H2; the separated gases leave through their own paths.
  5. Product conditioning removes entrained water/impurities according to specification; downstream compression/storage is a separate duty to include when claiming delivered-system efficiency.
  6. Overall,2H2O→2H2+O2; alkaline and solid-oxide half-reactions use different transported ions and must not be replaced blindly by PEM reactions.

Application / advantages

Renewable-powered electrolysis is one green-hydrogen route, subject to the applicable emissions/energy boundary; production follows specific electrical consumption.

Common mistake / conditions

H2/O2 separation, water purity, materials and control are safety-critical. This is not a DIY generation, wiring or pressurising procedure.

Common Mistake / શરતો

body.en:
Definition / principle

The separator, transported ion, water/steam feed and temperature requirements change with type; do not copy one cell diagram into every answer.

Understand why

Alkaline:electrodes work with a suitable alkaline electrolyte and separator; hydroxide ions move through the electrolyte from cathode to anode. The cathode forms hydrogen from water; the anode forms oxygen; gas separation and electrolyte handling need engineered control.

PEM:a solid proton membrane separates anode/cathode layers; water oxidation at anode supplies protons that cross to form hydrogen at cathode. Compactness and dynamic operation can be useful, but catalyst/material cost and water purity are important.

Solid-oxide electrolysis:a high-temperature ceramic cell commonly transports oxide ions; steam is reduced on the hydrogen-producing electrode and oxide ions move to the oxygen-producing electrode. Heat integration can lower the electrical share, but thermal cycling, sealing and durable materials are challenges.

Compare electricity plus heat on the stated boundary; less electricity alone does not prove lower total energy or greener production.

Definition / principle

Understand why

Productionkg/h=electrical inputkW divided by specific consumptionkWh/kg, on the same boundary.

Stoichiometry needs about9kgwater perkgH2; actual plant water intake includes treatment losses, cooling and site design and can be higher.

Efficiency onLHVbasis=H2LHVenergy output/electrical input; do not compare it directly to anHHVfigure without conversion.

Compression, purification and auxiliaries must be included if the claimed boundary is delivered hydrogen.

body.en:
Given and model

Illustrative plant electrical boundary100 kW, specific consumption50kWh/kgH2inclusive of the stated auxiliaries; H2LHV33.333kWh/kg.

Step-by-step solution

  1. Production=100/50=2 kg/h
  2. H2LHVoutput=2×33.333≈66.666 kW
  3. LHV efficiency≈66.666/100=66.666%
  4. Stoichiometric water≈2×9=18 kg/h

Common mistake / conditions

18 kg/his the reaction minimum approximation, not guaranteed total site water demand; downstream duties outside the given boundary are not included.

Definition / principle

A fuel cell continuously converts supplied fuel and oxidant into electrical energy, heat and reaction products.

Understand why

It is not a rechargeable battery storing all reactants internally; fuel supply and supporting equipment are needed.

Individual cells produceDCand are connected into a stack; net plant output subtracts auxiliary consumption from gross stack output.

Hydrogen/oxygen overall reactionH2+½O2→H2Oreleases energy; the pathway through separated half-reactions permits electrical work.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Electrolyte is a useful main basis; direct fuel route is an additional basis, not always a separate electrolyte family.

Understand why

PEMFC:polymer proton membrane, suited to responsive systems; AFC:alkaline electrolyte with fuel/air impurity constraints.

PAFC:phosphoric acid; MCFC:molten carbonate; SOFC:solid oxide; higher-temperature types can integrate useful heat but have thermal/material challenges.

DMFC uses methanol directly in a suitablePEM-family cell; do not imply every fuel cell uses the same fuel, electrolyte or operating temperature.

Compare electrolyte, charge carrier, fuel purity, start-up, temperature range, application and limitations rather than memorising names only.

Do all fuel cells carry protons through the electrolyte?

No. The transported ionic species depends on the cell chemistry.

h.en: 5.9.2 Fuel-cell types:electrolyte, ion path and application

body.en:
Definition / principle

Use electrolyte as the main basis and then compare each type by transported ion, fuel constraints and duty.

Understand why

PEMFC:polymer membrane, protons pass anode to cathode; clean hydrogen, water management and fast response suit vehicles and responsive power.

AFC:alkaline electrolyte transports hydroxide ions from cathode to anode; electrode/electrolyte arrangements differ from PEM and CO2 sensitivity requires suitable reactant conditioning.

PAFC:phosphoric-acid electrolyte conducts protons; higher-temperature stationary combined heat/power service is a common application, with slower thermal response than a typical low-temperature PEM system.

MCFC:molten-carbonate electrolyte transports carbonate ions cathode to anode; high-temperature operation supports heat integration but needs appropriate CO2-containing cathode supply and corrosion control.

SOFC:ceramic oxide electrolyte commonly transports oxygen ions cathode to anode; hot operation can support fuel processing/heat recovery, while sealing, thermal cycling and start-up are challenging.

DMFC:direct methanol oxidation in a suitable polymer-electrolyte cell releases CO2 at the anode; liquid fuel storage is convenient for some portable duties, but methanol crossover and efficiency are limitations.
body.gu:

Main basis electrolyte;પછી transported ion,fuel constraints,dutyથી દરેક type compare કરો.

કારણ સાથે સમજીએ

PEMFC:polymer membrane,protons anodeથી cathode;clean hydrogen,water management,fast responseથી vehicles,responsive power માટે.

MCFC:molten carbonateમાં carbonate ions cathodeથી anode;high-temperature heat integration,પણ suitable CO2-containing cathode supply,corrosion control જરૂરી.

SOFC:ceramic oxideમાં સામાન્ય oxygen ions cathodeથી anode;hot operation fuel processing/heat recovery આપે,પણ sealing,thermal cycling,start-up challenges.

body.en:
Definition / principle

UsePEMas the detailed representative cell; other electrolytes have different ionic paths.

Classification / types — basis first

  • Fuel cells are classified primarily by electrolyte:PEMFC, AFC, PAFC, MCFC, SOFC; DMFC identifies a direct-methanol fuel route within a suitable polymer-electrolyte family. PEM is the detailed representative, not the construction of every type.

Construction — each part and its purpose

  1. Anode catalyst promotes hydrogen oxidation; gas-diffusion layer spreads fuel and supports access to active sites.
  2. Cathode catalyst promotes oxygen reduction; its gas-diffusion layer supports air delivery and water removal.
  3. Polymer membrane conducts protons while normally blocking electrons and separating reactant gases.
  4. Bipolar plates and flow channels collect current and route gases; seals and clamping keep paths separated.
  5. Series-connected cells form a stack to obtain useful voltage; the stack is not an AC generator by itself.
  6. Hydrogen supply, air compressor/blower, cooling, water management, power electronics, sensors and controls are balance-of-plant equipment.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Hydrogen and oxygen-containing air enter separate anode/cathode flow channels.
  2. Anode:H2→2H+ +2e−; the catalyst enables oxidation without normal flame combustion.
  3. Protons move through hydrated membrane; electrons take the external circuit and deliver DC electrical work to a load.
  4. Cathode:1/2O2+2H+ +2e−→H2O; water forms on the cathode side in this representative chemistry.
  5. Cooling and water management remove heat/excess water while maintaining required membrane hydration.
  6. Continuous reactant supply sustains operation; gross stack electricity minus auxiliaries gives net system output on the stated boundary.

Application / advantages

Fuel-cell vehicles and responsive electrical systems; battery buffering can assist start-up and transients.

Common mistake / conditions

Fuel purity, catalyst cost, durability, water/thermal balance and H2 supply are limitations; tailpipe water does not prove green upstream production.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Electrons take the external circuit; protons pass through the membrane in this cell.

Understand why

Anode:H2→2H+ +2e−; the catalyst separates the hydrogen reaction into charge carriers.

Protons cross the membrane; electrons flow through the external load and deliver electrical power.

Cathode:½O2+2H+ +2e−→H2O; air supplies oxygen and water/heat are managed.

Inadequate hydration, flooding, contamination and thermal imbalance reduce performance; tailpipe water alone does not establish green upstream production.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Identify leak/ignition, pressure/cryogen and material hazards before selecting controls.

Understand why

Low ignition energy and leaks require engineered detection, ventilation, ignition control and isolation/shutdown.

Pressure/cryogenic hazards require rated components, compatible materials, relief and trained handling; oxygen systems have separate compatibility needs.

Hydrogen can embrittle susceptible materials and permeate seals; gas buoyancy does not guarantee safety in enclosed roof spaces.

Never use flame leak tests, improvised storage, DIYfilling or unapproved gas generation; follow authorised emergency procedures and trained supervision.

h.en: 5.11.2 Hydrogen vehicles and hybrid energy systems
h.gu: 5.11.2 Hydrogen Vehicles અને Hybrid Energy Systems

body.en:
Definition / principle

Separate fuel-cell electric vehicles from H2 combustion engines; both require approved storage and safety.

Understand why

FCEV path:H2 supply→fuel-cell stack/DCconversion→DCbus→inverter/motor→wheels.

A battery or supercapacitor in parallel buffers transients, supports start-up and stores regenerative braking energy; it is not simply a component in series after the stack.

H2ICEuses combustion and mechanical drive; it can formNOx and is not a fuel-cell vehicle.

Stationary hybrids combine renewables, electrolyser, storage, fuel cell and batteries; short/long-duration roles depend on efficiency, cost and service needs.

FCEV path:H2 supply→stack/DC conversion→DC bus→inverter/motor→wheels.

Parallel battery/supercapacitor transients buffer,start-up support,regenerative braking store કરે;ફક્ત stack પછી series component નહિ.

H2 ICE combustion,mechanical drive વાપરે;NOx બની શકે,FCEV નહિ.

Stationary hybridsમાં renewables,electrolyser,storage,fuel cell,batteries;roles efficiency,cost,service મુજબ.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Evaluate where H2 adds value compared with direct electrification and other alternatives.

Understand why

Potential roles include lower-emission industrial feedstock, reduction processes, some difficult-to-electrify transport and long-duration energy storage.

Challenges include renewable supply, delivered cost, water/site constraints, conversion losses, infrastructure, durable equipment and safety competence.

Claims must specify lifecycle boundary, purity, delivery form and useful output; production capacity announcements do not prove delivered low-carbon use.

Treat future pathways as conditional engineering options, not guaranteed dates, costs or universal replacements for batteries.

Is a fuel cell the same as a hydrogen engine?

No. Electrochemical conversion differs from combustion.
